Let me think about invariants. Consider the differences d_i = a_{i+1} - a_i. At a peak at i: d_{i-1} > 0, d_i < 0; update: a_i-- → d_{i-1} -= 1, d_i += 1. At a valley at i: d_{i-1} < 0, d_i > 0; update: d_{i-1} += 1, d_i -= 1.

So in either case, the update at position i is: d_{i-1} -= sign, d_i += sign, where sign = +1 for a peak, -1 for a valley. That is, the change in d: one unit moves from d_{i-1} to d_i, and d_{i-1} was positive (peak) — i.e., positive mass moves to the right… wait: peak: d_{i-1} -= 1 (decrease), d_i += 1 (increase). d_{i-1} > 0 is decreased, d_i < 0 is increased (toward 0). Valley: d_{i-1} += 1 (d_{i-1} < 0, toward 0), d_i -= 1 (d_i > 0, decreased).

So: at a peak (a + to − transition at i), 1 unit of positive mass moves from d_{i-1} to d_i. But d_i is negative, so the positive unit cancels the negative unit there. At a valley (a − to + transition), 1 unit of negative mass moves from d_{i-1} to d_i (d_{i-1} is negative, d_i is positive → cancellation).

Equivalently: |d| shrinks at ± transitions: at a peak, d_{i-1} (positive) decreases by 1, d_i (negative) increases by 1. At a valley, d_{i-1} (negative) increases by 1, d_i (positive) decreases by 1.

So the sign-change points (peaks/valleys) shrink the adjacent differences by 1 per pass, and when d_{i-1} or d_i reaches 0, the transition is resolved.

The key subtlety: all updates within a pass are simultaneous (snapshot t is computed at the start of the pass, all updates applied). In d-space, per-pass update: for each active site (based on start-of-pass values), d[i−1] −= sign(d[i−1]), d[i] −= sign(d[i]). If two sites both touch the same d[k], it gets two unit changes in one pass (which is what "rate 2" means). This is exactly what I modeled. And events (zeros) occur after integer passes since all rates are integer and initial values are integers. When d[k] reaches exactly 0 after a pass, subsequent passes have no site there. ✓

One more consideration: can a d[k] overshoot zero? E.g., d[k] = 1 with two sites active → −2 in one pass? A site fires only if sign change exists at start of pass, i.e., d[k] = 1 (say positive) and neighbor negative: one site contributes −1; the other site touching d[k] (on the other side) would require sign change on that side too: neighbor also negative → d[k]=1 with both neighbors negative: sites on both sides fire: d[k] −= 2 → d[k] = −1. Overshoot! Does that happen in our case? Note: each element can be both a peak and a valley... no wait, it can't. That means the array is monotonic non-decreasing or non-increasing... more precisely: between any two consecutive differences, a sign change cannot exist.
